title: Strict Roos comparison and integral completeness across a finite clopen cover
statement:
Fix the global field $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ and a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$ as in [def-pur-conventions]. Let $X$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $j_i:X_i\hookrightarrow X$, $i\in I$, be a finite pairwise disjoint open and closed cover [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Use the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site].

Fix a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-pur-conventions].

Write $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}=\varprojlim_n(A_{E,n})_X$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] and $r_i$ for restriction of its module sheaves and complexes [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. A strict tower consists of complexes $C_n$ and chain maps $t_n:C_{n+1}\to C_n$, with morphisms the compatible families of chain maps. Restriction and sectionwise product gluing are inverse equivalences on these strict towers. Restriction identifies termwise countable products with the component products, carries the endomorphism $(c_n)_n\mapsto(c_n-t_n(c_{n+1}))_n$ to the identical component formula, and induces a natural chain isomorphism
$$r_i\operatorname{Cone}(1-s_C)[-1]\cong\operatorname{Cone}(1-s_{r_iC})[-1].$$
This comparison is compatible with strict tower maps and their projections. On derived categories it preserves the derived-limit property, with its specified Roos triangle [def-weil-derived-limit]. In particular the actual reduction maps $K\to\operatorname{Res}_n(K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n})$ and the transitions restrict to the corresponding component maps [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction, def-weil-integral-reduction-tower].

Derived completeness [def-weil-derived-complete] is equivalent to derived completeness of every component, retaining the specified first map to the product in the Roos triangle. Membership in $D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] is equivalent to componentwise membership. Membership in $D^b_{ctf}(X,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] is likewise equivalent to componentwise membership. For both the cohomological supports of all positive reductions and their Tor amplitudes, any common bounds for the finite list of component bounds uniform in $n$ are uniform bounds on $X$.

The unbounded restriction equivalence therefore restricts to these two integral full subcategories. It preserves completed tensor products and their coefficient units as defined by the strict reduction towers in [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. For every finite coefficient-field extension $E\subset L$, it commutes naturally with the integral scalar extension of [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension], including the level maps to $A_{L,m}$ and their transitions. No canonical cone is asserted in a bare triangulated category: functoriality refers to the displayed strict complex model. All assertions include the empty partition.
